message.reasoning:
I'm planning JUnit 4 tests for the Element class, covering constructors with null tag validation, tagName handling, tag/block checks, id and attribute behavior, and dataset/parent access.

I'm continuing to map out test coverage for parent traversal, child collections filtered by node type, CSS select queries, append/prepend operations with null validation, insertion bounds checking, wrapping and sibling navigation including parentNode null cases, and Collector-based getter methods that should throw on empty input.

I'm also listing out text/class/attribute manipulation methods like className, hasClass, addClass/removeClass/toggleClass, val(), html(), toString(), equals/hashCode, and clone() as areas needing tests. For these, I'm planning to use Jsoup.parse() to build real Documents and Elements since that's the standard way to exercise navigation methods in jsoup's own test suite, checking whether the jsoup jar is actually available given the listed dependencies.

I'm sketching out a sequence of test methods covering constructor validation (null tag, empty baseUri, null/empty tag name throwing via Validate), tag name getters/setters, and tag object identity checks.

I'm also planning tests for block-vs-inline tag detection, attribute presence/absence, chained attr calls, dataset handling, and parent/parents traversal (including stopping at #root when parsed via Jsoup).

Continuing through child element access by index, filtering children() to exclude text nodes, out-of-bounds index exceptions, text node and data node (script content) handling, basic CSS select functionality, and various append/prepend/insert child operations with null checks, negative index handling, and bounds validation.

Then I move into testing HTML append/prepend operations, inserting before/after string nodes, emptying children, wrapping elements, and sibling element traversal methods - checking null-parent cases, sibling exclusion of self, and next/previous sibling retrieval at list boundaries.

For firstElementSibling, since parent.children() includes the element itself, it returns the first sibling only when there's more than one child, otherwise null - so I need to test both the single-child and multi-child cases.

Then I cover sibling index lookups (0 when no parent, correct index otherwise), lastElementSibling symmetry with firstElementSibling, validation that getElementsByTag throws on empty strings, basic tag lookups, and getElementById testing both the found and not-found branches.

I continue through class and attribute selectors, regex-based attribute and text matching including invalid regex throwing IllegalArgumentException, getAllElements, text extraction with br whitespace handling, ownText, hasText, script data extraction, className, and empty classNames.

I'm working out edge cases like className returning empty string when no class attribute exists, splitting that into classNames, then covering classNames mutators, hasClass case insensitivity, add/remove/toggleClass, val() for textarea versus other elements, html getter/setter, toString, equals/hashCode semantics (reference equality only), and clone behavior. Given the scope, I'll aim for a reasonably thorough but not exhaustive test class covering key branches, then move to writing the actual code with the necessary jsoup imports.

I'm confirming Validate.notNull and notEmpty throw IllegalArgumentException, which determines what exception type my tests should expect, then planning how to construct test fixtures like parsing a script tag to test data nodes.

Checking className() behavior: since attr() returns an empty string when the class attribute is absent, classNames() would end up splitting an empty string, which in Java produces an array containing a single empty string rather than an empty array.

Since the regex requires at least one character, splitting an empty string yields no matches, so the whole empty string becomes the sole element. That confirms classNames() on an element without a class attribute returns a Set containing just the empty string "" — a quirk worth testing explicitly.

Following that, hasClass("") would then evaluate to true against that set, which is an odd edge case but legitimately derived from the source logic, so I'll include it while noting it's an intentional quirk rather than a guess. Given the scope, I'll aim for a thorough but manageable test file, grouping related assertions into fewer methods to keep things organized without excessive verbosity.
